properties.role: Tide-reader and boatwoman at pier four; the only one who rows near the bell water
properties.played_as: Whispers as if the water might hear her, never meets the party's eyes, keeps her gaze on the tide line; shrugs and goes back to mending her net. Dockhands say her name both Sela and Sella.
properties.wants: To avoid the water at night; will row the party by day for two silver.
properties.knows: Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang, forty years ago; her grandmother said the water came up warm.

sources.quote: Sela Thorn. I read the tides. I'll row you, but not at night. Never at night.
She talks in a whisper, like the water might hear her, and she never once looks you in the eye.

changes.why: New NPC voiced by the GM who will row the party.

sources.quote: There's a woman sitting on an upturned skiff, mending a net.
you're standing at the end of pier four looking for a boat.

changes.why: Sela works at the docks, pier four.

change.name: Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang

properties.statement: Saltmere Mine flooded forty years ago on the same night the bell first rang, and the water came up warm.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: World fact told by Sela that ties the mine to the bell.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang.

changes.why: The fact is about Saltmere Mine.

properties.details_shown: Up the cliff path, about an hour's walk from Gullwick. A black mouth in the chalk, half-rotted timber frame, a rusted cart on its side. Warm air smells of church and old candle wax. Thirty paces in the tunnel is flooded with warm black water; wet hymn-book pages float on it and cling to the walls.
properties.state: Flooded, with warm water; closed for forty years.

sources.quote: The air coming out of it is warm and smells like a church, like old candle wax.
About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch.

changes.why: The party visited and saw the mine's current state.

properties.what_changed: In the flooded Saltmere Mine Teo found a wet hymn page with "M. Brand" pencilled in the margin; Teo says it is Mira's handwriting, so she was there.

sources.quote: A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".
That's Mira. That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.

changes.why: First physical trace of Mira; the handwriting identification is Teo's own claim.

change.name: Is Maren Vosk in the choir?

properties.what_is_open: Vessa and Oren suspect harbor-master Maren Vosk of being in the cult and running the Hollow Choir. No evidence at the table; the GM did not confirm it.

sources.quote: Okay, I bet the harbor-master is behind all this. Maren wanted us gone from day one. She's in the cult, I'm calling it.
Yeah, Maren is totally running the choir.

changes.why: Players' theory is a new open thread, kept as a guess.

sources.quote: Maren wanted us gone from day one.

properties.details_shown: Sank into the bay with its bell. At low water the roof sticks out of the bay: the bell tower and two broken arches, seaweed hanging from the stones. At midnight, pale shapes stand in rows on the chapel floor under the water, like a congregation, and vanish when the bell stops.
properties.state: Bell tower and two arches visible at low water.

sources.quote: The drowned chapel's roof sticks out of the bay at low water, just the bell tower and two broken arches.
Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation.

changes.why: The party saw the chapel and the congregation shapes.

sources.quote: (to himself) That's the choir clock at three of six.

changes.why: The GM advanced the hidden clock from 2 to 3.

properties.statement: Local fishermen say the Kelp Mother pulls children who stand too close to the water down by the ankles. Only a rumor; the GM did not confirm it.

sources.quote: The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.
That's what the fishermen say.

changes.why: Local belief told by fishermen, kept as a rumor.

properties.details_shown: Tavern by the docks. A fire going; smells of tar and fish stew.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.

changes.why: New place where the party rests.

properties.played_as: Huge, red-bearded, laughs at his own jokes, wipes the same mug the whole time he talks. Friendly: feeds the party on the house.
properties.knows: Has known Maren Vosk for thirty years.

sources.quote: Bram is huge, red beard, laughs at his own jokes, and he wipes the same mug the whole time he talks to you.
You lot went to the shore at midnight? Brave or stupid. On the house, either way.

changes.why: New NPC voiced by the GM.

sources.quote: The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.

change.name: Maren Vosk lost a brother to the bay

properties.statement: Harbor-master Maren Vosk lost a brother to the bay, according to Bram, who calls her sharp-tongued with a good heart.

sources.quote: Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: Bram's account of Maren's past, relevant to the suspicion thread.

sources.quote: She lost a brother to that bay.

properties.next_step: Tomorrow at first light Sela rows the party out and they dive to the drowned chapel at low tide, with rope and a second lantern. Teo's reasoning: Mira wrote in the hymn book and the chapel is where the hymns came from.

sources.quote: So tomorrow, first light, Sela rows us out and we dive to the chapel at low tide. I'll buy rope and a second lantern tonight.
Agreed. Tomorrow we dive.

changes.why: The party's agreed plan is the next step on the bell thread.
